## A. BINDING MUST-FIXES (Methodology reconciler — must be addressed in v2)

### MF1 — Section scoping must not qualify a line via a document-spanning H1

**Defect.** `_headings` (verify_plan.py:674-695) ends a heading's span at the
next same-or-higher heading. The house plan template has exactly ONE H1, so its
span is the WHOLE DOCUMENT. The sketched `_c68_sections_ok` accepts a line if
ANY enclosing heading matches, so an experiment plan whose H1 carries
`gate|decision|hypothes|success|kill|verdict` — e.g. `# Plan: decision-gate
cleanup`, or a realistic descendant `# Plan: #22xx — harm-rate decision-gate
rework` — makes EVERY §2/§8 line margin-eligible.

Traced false positive: margins harvested {2 (the real, valid gate), 30 (a Risks
quotation of a sibling's broken margin, eligible only via the H1)}, bmax = 20%
→ 30 ≥ 20 → **WARN on a healthy plan**.

**Why binding (three grounds the "inherited idiom" defence does not answer).**
(a) c13 (:2014) and c28 (:5286) DO use the byte-identical any-enclosing walk —
that Claude claim is accurate — but their comments promise only "under-trigger
fails safe" and never claim quoted-line immunity, whereas c68's §4.1 comment
claims categorically that "a §2/§8 line QUOTING a broken sibling margin
therefore never fires." The precedent does not license the stronger claim. The
§7 kill criterion is ZERO FPs and §0 stakes the design on it, yet the §6.3
calibration corpus structurally cannot exercise this class (only 3 A1/A2 files
exist, all incident-family — the survivor-population gap). c68's exposure is
ELEVATED over c13/c28: its trigger vocabulary is exactly what descendant plans
quote in §2 recaps of the founding incident, against baselines (~9.7%) below the
quoted 10pp margin. (b) No downstream net: the plan explicitly prescribes
`any(enclosing heading)` and pins the neutral-H1 negative, so a plan-adherent
